headline: JAGUAR CONFIRMS HIGH-GRADE FAINA ZONE AT TURMALINA — 11.88 g/t Au OVER 5.4m AS Q2 PRODUCTION SURGES 19% TO 13,057 OZ (TSX: JAG)
snippet: Jaguar Mining Inc. (TSX: JAG) reported two milestones on July 27: Q2 2026 gold production of 13,057 oz — up 19% year-over-year — driven by the accelerating Turmalina mine ramp-up, and initial drill results from the Faina orebody returning 11.88 g/t gold over 5.39 metres, confirming mineralization continuity in a zone that was inaccessible until underground development resumed in March 2026. Turmalina delivered 3,994 oz at 2.94 g/t while Pilar added 9,063 oz at 3.30 g/t; Jaguar held $74.8 million cash at June 30 with full financial results due mid-August.

headline: FOMC EVE: GOLD SAYS THE HOLD IS ALREADY PRICED IN — SILVER SAYS THE MARKET IS WRONG, AND THE 70:1 RATIO AGREES
snippet: GoldSilver.com's pre-FOMC analysis finds gold at $4,082 has already fully priced in a Fed hold while silver at $59-60 — still suppressed by the 70:1 gold-silver ratio — signals the market does not share gold's confidence. With the June FOMC minutes revealing a 9-to-8 committee split and roughly 20% futures probability of a July 29 hike, the divergence creates an asymmetric setup for silver: a confirmed hold on July 29 releases both the rate-hold premium and ratio normalization simultaneously, while gold captures only the marginal re-confirmation.

headline: COPPER NEAR US RECORD AS CHILE'S STORM-HIT OUTPUT MOUNTS AND CHINA'S PHYSICAL IMPORT GAUGE HITS ONE-YEAR HIGH
snippet: Copper climbed on July 27 as fresh Chinese physical demand — the key Yangshan import premium hitting a one-year high — combined with a growing tally of weather-related Chilean output losses. Chile's May production fell 12.94% year-on-year, Antofagasta's H1 was down 9.5%, Lundin Mining's Caserones suspended July 18 after a winter storm cut power, and a new atmospheric river is forecast to deliver up to 150mm across the central copper belt with Codelco estimating El Teniente losses of approximately US$7.5 million per day. SHFE inventories are down 82% since May; Comex is within 2% of its US all-time record.

headline: AGNICO EAGLE REPORTS ON FOMC DAY — $2.89 EPS AND $3.78B REVENUE EXPECTED, 49% YoY EPS GROWTH AT $4,080 GOLD (NYSE: AEM)
snippet: Agnico Eagle Mines (NYSE: AEM) releases Q2 2026 results after market close on July 29 — the same session as the Federal Reserve decision and Kinross Gold's Q2 report. Analyst consensus is US$2.89 EPS and US$3.775 billion revenue, implying 49% year-over-year EPS growth. Agnico beat Q1 2026 estimates by $0.21 (reported $3.39 vs $3.19) and generated record quarterly operating margins at $4,861/oz realized gold; Q2 margins will compress to approximately $4,051/oz realized against guidance AISC of $1,175-$1,225/oz — still historically wide. The world's third-largest gold miner has paid dividends every year since 1983.

headline: PHENOM SPUDS FIRST HOLES AT DOBBIN GOLD IN NEVADA'S CARLIN BELT — 2.1KM ANOMALY UP TO 2.73 g/t Au TARGETED (TSXV: PHNM)
snippet: Phenom Resources Corp. (TSXV: PHNM) commenced core drilling on July 27 at the Dobbin Gold Project in Nevada's Monitor Range, targeting a 2.1-kilometre-long by 200-metre-wide northeast-trending gold-in-soils anomaly with surface values from 0.1 g/t to 2.73 g/t gold, 85 miles south of Eureka. The geological setting shows Carlin-type characteristics — lower-plate Paleozoic carbonates, near-surface gold, feeder structure, and pathfinder metals — with the permit allowing up to 26 core holes across 13 drill sites plus mechanical trenches. At $4,082 gold, Nevada's royalty regime and established infrastructure make this scale of anomaly worth first-pass drill testing.

headline: ZODIAC GOLD DRILLS THIRD TARGET ON ITS 16KM LIBERIA GOLD TREND — 3,000m INAUGURAL PROGRAM AT LEWIS UNDERWAY (TSXV: ZAU)
snippet: Zodiac Gold Inc. (TSXV: ZAU) commenced up to 3,000 metres of inaugural diamond drilling at the Lewis target on its Todi Gold Project in Liberia on July 21, announced July 27, marking the third systematic target tested along the company's 16-kilometre Monterra Trend. Lewis covers a 1.8-kilometre east-west gold-in-soil anomaly in previously untested ground on the same structural corridor as the flagship Arthington discovery. The results will be a key test of whether the Monterra Trend's gold endowment extends district-wide beyond the Arthington zone.

headline: LITHIUM SINKS TO 5-MONTH LOW AS BALD HILL, CATL, AND FINNISS RETURN — MINE RESTARTS STOKE 2027 GLUT FEARS
snippet: Lithium prices fell to a five-month low in July 2026 as three suspended operations returned to production simultaneously: Mineral Resources' Bald Hill spodumene mine delivered its first concentrate after an 18-month shutdown, CATL's Jianxiawo — one of the world's largest lithium mines — cleared safety approvals to resume, and Core Lithium restarted Finniss. Despite Chinese battery production up 55.2% year-over-year (191.7 GWh in May), markets are pricing a 2027 supply surplus. Lithium had rallied 98% year-over-year entering July on spodumene reaching approximately US$2,800/tonne.

headline: LEVERAGE CUTS BOTH WAYS: ALAMOS -25%, EQUINOX -28% IN JULY AS GOLD SLIDES FROM $5,318 — WHAT RETAIL INVESTORS MISSED
snippet: A July 2026 analysis documents how gold's 24% decline from its $5,318 all-time high to the $4,035 intra-month low translated into 25-28% equity drops for senior miners Alamos Gold and Equinox Gold — with GDX off 15.54% in June alone — as fixed costs, guidance cuts, and investor mood amplified the metal's decline. Franco-Nevada, Wheaton, and Agnico Eagle remain in the lowest historical percentiles on price-to-NAV and price-to-cash flow, a setup that has historically preceded strong sector re-ratings when gold price direction stabilises. The ceasefire bounce has begun recovering the damage, but the piece serves as an honest primer on mining equity risk for retail investors attracted by the leverage narrative.

headline: UKRAINE APPROVES UAH555M LOAN TO BOOST URANIUM ORE EXTRACTION AT EASTERN MINING PLANT
snippet: Ukraine's cabinet approved a UAH555 million (approximately US$12.4 million) state loan to the Eastern Mining and Processing Plant — Ukraine's primary domestic uranium ore producer — to increase extraction and uranium oxide concentrate production. Ukraine's 15 operating nuclear reactors supply approximately 25% of national electricity, making domestic uranium a strategic priority as the ongoing conflict disrupts legacy supply chains. At $86/lb uranium spot and with the U.S. Section 232 review still pending, incremental Western-aligned uranium production carries geopolitical weight well beyond its headline tonnage.

headline: GOLDGROUP NAMES JAVIER REYES INTERIM CEO AS NEWLY MERGED $372M MEXICO GOLD COMPANY BEGINS PERMANENT LEADERSHIP SEARCH (TSXV: GORO)
snippet: Goldgroup Mining (TSXV: GORO) — the multi-mine Mexico gold producer formed by the July 2026 merger with Gold Resource Corporation in a US$372 million business combination — announced July 27 that Javier Reyes has been appointed Interim CEO while the board conducts a comprehensive search for a permanent executive. The combined company spans the Cerro Prieto and San Francisco mines in Sonora, the Don David mine in Oaxaca, and the Back Forty project in Michigan. The transition signals the board is taking time to identify the right permanent leader for the enlarged asset base rather than defaulting to either predecessor company's management team.
